results.name: common_digit_far_bonus
results.description: Among multi-example sets, for targets more than 10 from every example and not ending in any example's final digit, yes-rate when the target contains a digit written in every example minus yes-rate otherwise; observed above null means the model under-produces digit-containment generalisation.
results.code:
# name: common_digit_far_bonus
# description: Among multi-example sets, for targets more than 10 from every example and not ending in any example's final digit, yes-rate when the target contains a digit written in every example minus yes-rate otherwise; observed above null means the model under-produces digit-containment generalisation.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    ok = ~np.isnan(ex)
    def mask(v):
        v = v.astype(np.int64)
        tensd = (v // 10) % 10
        m = np.left_shift(1, v % 10)
        m = m | np.where(v >= 10, np.left_shift(1, tensd), 0)
        m = m | np.where(v >= 100, 2, 0)
        return m
    exm = np.where(ok, mask(np.nan_to_num(ex, nan=1.0)), 1023)
    common = np.bitwise_and.reduce(exm, axis=1)
    tm = mask(t)
    has = (common & tm) != 0
    n = ok.sum(axis=1)
    dist = np.where(ok, np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), np.inf).min(axis=1)
    last = np.where(ok, (np.nan_to_num(ex) % 10) == (t % 10)[:, None], False).any(axis=1)
    m = (n >= 2) & (dist > 10) & ~last
    a, b = m & has, m & ~has
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: set_size_yes_gap
results.description: Yes-rate for non-example targets after 4-example sets minus after 1-example sets; observed above null means the model over-tightens generalisation as examples accumulate (size-principle too strong), below means too weak.
results.code:
# name: set_size_yes_gap
# description: Yes-rate for non-example targets after 4-example sets minus after 1-example sets; observed above null means the model over-tightens generalisation as examples accumulate (size-principle too strong), below means too weak.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    ok = ~np.isnan(ex)
    n = ok.sum(axis=1)
    inset = np.where(ok, ex == t[:, None], False).any(axis=1)
    a = (n == 4) & ~inset
    b = (n == 1) & ~inset
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: partial_last_digit_match_bonus
results.description: Among multi-example sets whose examples do NOT all share a final digit, yes-rate for non-example targets ending in the same digit as at least one example minus yes-rate for targets matching no example's final digit; observed above null means the model under-produces feature-wise (partial) final-digit similarity.
results.code:
# name: partial_last_digit_match_bonus
# description: Among multi-example sets whose examples do NOT all share a final digit, yes-rate for non-example targets ending in the same digit as at least one example minus yes-rate for targets matching no example's final digit; observed above null means the model under-produces feature-wise (partial) final-digit similarity.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    ok = ~np.isnan(ex)
    n = ok.sum(axis=1)
    exl = np.nan_to_num(ex) % 10
    first = exl[:, :1]
    allsame = np.where(ok, exl == first, True).all(axis=1)
    match = np.where(ok, exl == (t % 10)[:, None], False).any(axis=1)
    inset = np.where(ok, ex == t[:, None], False).any(axis=1)
    m = (n >= 2) & ~allsame & ~inset
    a, b = m & match, m & ~match
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: near_vs_mid_distance_gap
results.description: Yes-rate for non-example targets 1-2 from the nearest example minus yes-rate for targets 5-10 away; observed below null means people do not show the steep near-neighbour similarity gradient the model predicts (and vice versa).
results.code:
# name: near_vs_mid_distance_gap
# description: Yes-rate for non-example targets 1-2 from the nearest example minus yes-rate for targets 5-10 away; observed below null means people do not show the steep near-neighbour similarity gradient the model predicts (and vice versa).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    dist = np.where(~np.isnan(ex), np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), np.inf).min(axis=1)
    a = (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 2)
    b = (dist >= 5) & (dist <= 10)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: same_decade_near_bonus
results.description: Among non-example targets 1-9 away from the nearest example and sharing no final digit with any example, yes-rate when the target shares a tens digit (decade) with some example minus yes-rate when it does not; observed above null means the model under-produces a decade-sharing bonus.
results.code:
# name: same_decade_near_bonus
# description: Among non-example targets 1-9 away from the nearest example and sharing no final digit with any example, yes-rate when the target shares a tens digit (decade) with some example minus yes-rate when it does not; observed above null means the model under-produces a decade-sharing bonus.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    ok = ~np.isnan(ex)
    diff = np.where(ok, np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), np.inf)
    dist = diff.min(axis=1)
    last = np.where(ok, (np.nan_to_num(ex) % 10) == (t % 10)[:, None], False).any(axis=1)
    tens = np.where(ok, (np.nan_to_num(ex) // 10) == (t // 10)[:, None], False).any(axis=1)
    m = (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 9) & ~last
    a, b = m & tens, m & ~tens
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: inside_vs_outside_range_gap
results.description: Among multi-example sets, yes-rate for non-example targets inside the examples' [min, max] range minus yes-rate for targets outside it; observed above null means the model under-produces interval-like (range-filling) generalisation, below means it over-produces it.
results.code:
# name: inside_vs_outside_range_gap
# description: Among multi-example sets, yes-rate for non-example targets inside the examples' [min, max] range minus yes-rate for targets outside it; observed above null means the model under-produces interval-like (range-filling) generalisation, below means it over-produces it.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    ok = ~np.isnan(ex)
    n = ok.sum(axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    inset = np.where(ok, ex == t[:, None], False).any(axis=1)
    m = (n >= 2) & ~inset
    inside = (t >= mn) & (t <= mx)
    a, b = m & inside, m & ~inside
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[a].mean() - y[b].mean())

results.name: between_set_yes_dispersion
results.description: Standard deviation across sets (those with at least 40 non-example-target trials) of the per-set yes-rate; observed above null means the model under-produces how differently people treat different sets (too homogeneous), below means it exaggerates set differences.
results.code:
# name: between_set_yes_dispersion
# description: Standard deviation across sets (those with at least 40 non-example-target trials) of the per-set yes-rate; observed above null means the model under-produces how differently people treat different sets (too homogeneous), below means it exaggerates set differences.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    inset = np.where(~np.isnan(ex), ex == t[:, None], False).any(axis=1)
    d = df.loc[~inset, ["number_set", "rating"]]
    g = d.groupby("number_set")["rating"].agg(["mean", "size"])
    g = g[g["size"] >= 40]
    if len(g) < 2:
        return 0.0
    return float(g["mean"].astype(float).std())
